findings.title: Bidder Eligibility: Only Lot 2 Hardware Contractors
findings.fact: RFQ 23-01 is only distributed to Contractors holding an award for Lot 2 – Hardware under the Manufacturer Umbrella Contract. Quotes will only be accepted from Lot 2 Contractors; Resellers are not eligible and will be disqualified.
findings.business_implication: Only contractors with an existing Lot 2 Hardware award under the Manufacturer Umbrella Contract can participate. Resellers are automatically disqualified, so any bid from a reseller will be rejected.
findings.action_recommendation: Confirm that your company holds a valid Lot 2 Hardware award under the Manufacturer Umbrella Contract before investing time in preparing a response. If you are a reseller, do not attempt to bid as you will be disqualified.

quotes.quote: Quotes from Resellers will not be accepted. Contractors must have an award for Lot 2 to bid on this RFQ.

RFQ 23-01 is only being distributed to Contractors holding an award for Lot 2 – Hardware under the Manufacturer Umbrella Contract (“Contractors”). Quotes under RFQ 23-01 will only be accepted from Lot 2 Contractors on the Manufacturer Umbrella Contract; Resellers are not eligible to respond and any bids from a Reseller will be disqualified.

findings.title: Products Must Be on Manufacturer Umbrella Contract Price List
findings.fact: All proposed products (Standard Configuration, Required Products, Additional Products) must be on the Contractor's Manufacturer Umbrella Contract Lot 2 - Hardware price list at the time of the RFQ Submission due date.
findings.business_implication: Any product not listed on your Manufacturer Umbrella Contract price list by the submission deadline cannot be included in your bid. This could limit your ability to offer certain configurations or products.
findings.action_recommendation: Review your current Manufacturer Umbrella Contract price list to ensure all products you intend to propose are listed. If any products are missing, submit a contract modification request well before the RFQ submission due date, indicating they are for RFQ 23-01.

quotes.quote: All Products proposed as part of the Standard Configuration and Products proposed for Required Products, as well as any Additional Products, must be on the Contractor's Manufacturer Umbrella Contract Lot 2 - Hardware price list at the time of the RFQ Submission due date.
All proposed SKUs for Products offered must be on the Contractor’s approved Manufacturer Umbrella Contract price list prior to the RFQ Submission due date for RFQ 23-01.

findings.title: Pre-qualification: Must Hold Manufacturer Umbrella Contract Lot 2
findings.fact: Bidders must already hold an award for Lot 2 – Hardware under the Manufacturer Umbrella Contract to be eligible to bid.
findings.business_implication: This is a mandatory pre-qualification. Without a Lot 2 award, you cannot participate, and any bid submitted will be rejected.
findings.action_recommendation: Verify that your company has an active Lot 2 Hardware award under the Manufacturer Umbrella Contract. If not, do not attempt to bid; instead, consider partnering with an eligible contractor or pursuing other opportunities.

quotes.quote: Contractors must have an award for Lot 2 to bid on this RFQ.
RFQ 23-01 is only being distributed to Contractors holding an award for Lot 2 – Hardware under the Manufacturer Umbrella Contract (“Contractors”).

findings.title: Mandatory EPEAT Certification for Products
findings.fact: Desktops, laptops, and computer monitors must have EPEAT Gold certification at time of award, except Chromebooks which require EPEAT Silver.
findings.business_implication: Products offered must meet specific environmental certification standards. Failure to meet these requirements could result in disqualification of your bid or non-compliance with the contract.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure that all proposed desktops, laptops, and monitors have the required EPEAT Gold certification, and Chromebooks have EPEAT Silver. Verify certifications with manufacturers and include only compliant products in your bid.

quotes.quote: Desktops, laptops, and computer monitors provided under any resulting Agreement are required to have achieved a minimum certification of EPEAT Gold at the time of award with the exception of the three Chromebook Configurations (Chromebook Low, Chromebook with Touchscreen and Chromebook with Touchscreen – 14”). Chromebook Standard Configurations will be required to meet a minimum certification of EPEAT Silver at the time of award.

findings.title: Pre-qualification via Manufacturer Umbrella Contract
findings.fact: Contractors must already hold a Manufacturer Umbrella Contract with OGS to be eligible to respond to this RFQ.
findings.business_implication: This reinforces the requirement that only existing Manufacturer Umbrella Contract holders can bid. It also means that the terms and conditions of your existing contract will apply, along with any additional terms in this RFQ.
findings.action_recommendation: Confirm that your Manufacturer Umbrella Contract is active and in good standing. Review the terms and conditions of both your umbrella contract and this RFQ to ensure you can comply with all requirements.

quotes.quote: All Additional Products proposed by a Contractor on Attachment A – Technical Response and Attachment C – Financial Response must first be on Contractor’s approved Manufacturer Umbrella Contract price list.

The terms and conditions of the Contractor’s Manufacturer Umbrella Contract including any Amendments and the additional terms and conditions set forth in this RFQ 23-01, Section 7, Terms and Conditions govern any resulting award under RFQ 23-01.

findings.title: Bid Validity Period
findings.fact: Quotes must remain valid for at least 120 calendar days from the RFQ submission due date.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must commit to holding its pricing and terms for a minimum of 120 days, which may expose it to market fluctuations and cost changes during that period. This long validity period also means the bidder must ensure its internal approvals and pricing strategies account for potential extended commitment.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure that pricing and terms are set with a buffer to remain competitive and viable for at least 120 days. Obtain internal approvals for this extended validity period and monitor market conditions to mitigate risks.

quotes.quote: Quotes and pricing submitted in response to RFQ 23-01 must remain open and valid for at least 120 calendar days from the date that RFQ Submissions are due, unless the time for making an award is extended by mutual consent of OGS and the Contractor.

findings.title: Formatting and Envelope Rules (e.g., two-cover system)
findings.fact: Submissions must be on two USB flash drives, clearly labeled, and packaged/sealed. The submission must include Attachment A, Attachment D, and the Manufacturer Information Page.
findings.business_implication: Non-compliance with the strict submission format and packaging requirements could lead to disqualification. The bidder must ensure that all required documents are included on two USB drives, properly labeled, and sealed to avoid rejection.
findings.action_recommendation: Prepare two USB flash drives with all required documents (Attachment A, Attachment D, and Manufacturer Information Page) in the specified format. Double-check labeling and packaging, and ensure the drives are not password-protected and are readable. Follow the submission instructions precisely to avoid disqualification.

quotes.quote: Two (2) digital storage devices (USB flash drive), clearly labeled, shall contain the following documents, completed in their entirety: • Attachment A – Technical Response • Attachment D – Issue Escalation Plan • Manufacturer Information Page (Last page of this Document)
Each RFQ Submission should be packaged, sealed and submitted to the location stated below.

findings.title: Technical Response is Pass/Fail
findings.fact: The Technical Response is evaluated on a Pass/Fail basis, not scored.
findings.business_implication: Since the technical response is pass/fail, the bidder must ensure that its technical proposal fully meets all requirements without any deficiencies. There is no partial credit, so any missing or non-compliant element could result in disqualification regardless of the financial offer.
findings.action_recommendation: Thoroughly review the technical requirements and ensure that Attachment A, Attachment D, and the Manufacturer Information Page are complete and compliant. Pay close attention to all mandatory components and avoid any deviations that could render the bid non-responsive.

quotes.quote: Technical Response (Attachment A – Technical Response, Attachment D – Issue Escalation Plan, and Manufacturer Information Page): Pass/Fail

findings.title: Financial Response is 100% of evaluation
findings.fact: The Financial Response constitutes 100% of the evaluation weight.
findings.business_implication: The award decision will be based solely on the financial proposal, assuming the technical response passes. This means the bidder's pricing strategy is the critical factor for winning the contract. Competitive pricing is essential, but it must also be sustainable and profitable.
findings.action_recommendation: Focus on developing a highly competitive financial offer that maximizes the total financial score. Analyze the cost structure and consider pricing strategies that balance competitiveness with profitability. Ensure that all pricing components are accurately completed and aligned with the required products and services.

quotes.quote: Financial Response : 100%

findings.title: Financial scoring breakdown
findings.fact: Total Financial Score is based on lowest cost with points weighted as: Standard Configuration 50 points, Required Products (Warranty/Services 15 points, Components 30 points, Peripherals 5 points).
findings.business_implication: The financial evaluation is heavily weighted towards the standard configuration (50 points) and components (30 points), indicating that pricing on these items will have the most significant impact on the total score. The bidder must prioritize competitive pricing on these high-weight categories to maximize its chances of winning.
findings.action_recommendation: Allocate pricing efforts strategically: ensure that the standard configuration and components are priced competitively, as they carry the most weight. Also, review warranty/services and peripherals pricing to ensure they are competitive but not at the expense of the higher-weighted items. Use the scoring breakdown to optimize the overall financial offer.

quotes.quote: Total Financial Score is based on lowest cost and the points are weighted as follows: • Standard Configuration - 50 points • Required Products o Warranty/Services - 15 points o Components - 30 points o Peripherals - 5 points

findings.title: Award based on highest Total Financial Score
findings.fact: Awards are made to the responsive and responsible Contractor(s) with the highest Total Financial Score per Configuration that meets all specified technical requirements.
findings.business_implication: The award is determined solely by the financial score, which is based on lowest cost. This means that even if a bidder meets all technical requirements, they will only win if their pricing is the most competitive. The financial score is weighted heavily on standard configuration (50 points) and required products (50 points), so pricing strategy is critical.
findings.action_recommendation: Bidders should conduct a thorough cost analysis to ensure their pricing is competitive for each configuration they intend to bid on. They should also consider offering aggressive pricing on both standard configurations and required products to maximize their Total Financial Score.

quotes.quote: Awards will be made to the responsive and responsible Contractor(s) with the highest Total Financial Score per Configuration that meets all the specified technical requirements.

findings.title: Stage 2 Technical Evaluation - SKU verification
findings.fact: In Stage 2, proposed SKUs must be on the Contractor's approved Manufacturer Umbrella Contract price list; any configuration with a SKU not on the price list may not proceed further.
findings.business_implication: This is a strict gatekeeper: if any SKU in a configuration is not on the approved price list, that configuration will be disqualified from further evaluation. This means bidders must ensure that every SKU they propose is already listed on their Manufacturer Umbrella Contract price list before submission.
findings.action_recommendation: Bidders should verify that all SKUs they intend to propose are on their approved Manufacturer Umbrella Contract price list well before the submission deadline. If any SKU is missing, they should initiate a contract modification request promptly, as OGS will prioritize such requests for this RFQ.

quotes.quote: All proposed SKUs for proposed products offered in Attachment A – Technical Response must be on the Contractor’s approved Manufacturer Umbrella Contract price list. Any Configuration that contains a SKU that is not included on the Manufacturer’s Umbrella Contract price list may not proceed further in the evaluation process.

findings.title: Stage 3 Financial Evaluation - only for those passing technical
findings.fact: Only Contractors whose Standard Configuration specifications and Required Products pass review will proceed to the financial evaluation.
findings.business_implication: This means that technical compliance is a prerequisite for financial evaluation. Bidders cannot rely on low pricing to compensate for technical deficiencies; they must first pass the technical review to even be considered for the financial score.
findings.action_recommendation: Bidders should prioritize technical compliance in their submission. They should thoroughly review the technical requirements for each configuration and ensure that all proposed products meet the specifications. Any deviations could result in disqualification from the financial evaluation.

quotes.quote: Only Contractors whose Standard Configuration specifications and Required Products pass review, as determined by OGS, will proceed to the evaluation of Attachment C – Financial Response for those specific Configurations.

findings.title: Mandatory offerings - all components and required products
findings.fact: For each configuration bid, bidders must offer all components within the Standard Configuration and all Required Products; failure to complete all required fields may result in rejection.
findings.business_implication: This is a mandatory requirement: bidders must provide a complete offering for each configuration they bid on. Incomplete submissions, such as missing components or required products, will be rejected without further review. This emphasizes the need for meticulous attention to detail in the submission.
findings.action_recommendation: Bidders should use a checklist to ensure that all components and required products are included for each configuration they intend to bid on. They should also double-check that all required fields in Attachment A and Attachment C are completed accurately and fully before submission.

quotes.quote: FOR EACH CONFIGURATION BID, BIDDERS MUST OFFER ALL COMPONENTS WITHIN THE STANDARD CONFIGURATION AND ALL REQUIRED PRODUCTS . Failure to complete all required fields in Attachment A – Technical Response or Attachment C – Financial Response may result in rejection of the RFQ Submission without further review.

findings.title: Disqualification conditions
findings.fact: Disqualification conditions include: bids from Resellers are disqualified; failure to provide fully completed documents may result in rejection; any configuration with a SKU not on the price list may not proceed; failure to complete all required fields may result in rejection.
findings.business_implication: There are multiple strict disqualification conditions that bidders must avoid. Being a reseller is an automatic disqualification, so only eligible Lot 2 Contractors can bid. Additionally, incomplete documentation, missing SKUs, or incomplete fields can lead to rejection. This underscores the importance of compliance with all submission requirements.
findings.action_recommendation: Bidders should confirm their eligibility as a Lot 2 Contractor and not bid as a reseller. They should also implement a rigorous review process to ensure all documents are fully completed, all SKUs are on the price list, and all required fields are filled. It may be beneficial to have a second person review the submission before finalizing.

quotes.quote: Quotes under RFQ 23-01 will only be accepted from Lot 2 Contractors on the Manufacturer Umbrella Contract; Resellers are not eligible to respond and any bids from a Reseller will be disqualified.

findings.title: Technical Evaluation Criteria
findings.fact: Only items with mandatory specifications will be evaluated in the Technical Evaluation; additional items are reviewed only for inclusion in Lot 2 of the Manufacturer Umbrella Contract price list.
findings.business_implication: The technical evaluation focuses only on mandatory items, so additional items do not affect the technical score but must be on the approved price list to be included.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure all mandatory specifications are fully met and that any additional items proposed are already on the Manufacturer Umbrella Contract price list to avoid removal from the submission.

quotes.quote: Only items that have a mandatory specification will be evaluated in the Technical Evaluation; additional items needed to create the Standard Configuration listed in Section A of Attachment A- Technical Response will be reviewed only to determine if the items are included in Lot 2 of the Contractor’s Manufacturer Umbrella Contract price list.

findings.title: Financial Evaluation Includes Required Product Discounts
findings.fact: The discount percentages bid on Required Products will be factored into the Total Financial Score.
findings.business_implication: Aggressive discounts on Required Products can improve the financial score and increase chances of award.
findings.action_recommendation: Strategically set competitive discount percentages for Required Products to maximize the Total Financial Score while maintaining profitability.

quotes.quote: Contractors are encouraged to aggressively discount their pricing for their Required Products, as the pricing will be factored in the Total Financial Score.

findings.title: Disqualification for Non-Conformance
findings.fact: OGS may disqualify any Contractor whose quote fails to conform to the requirements of the RFQ.
findings.business_implication: Non-conformance with any RFQ requirement can lead to disqualification, risking loss of the opportunity.
findings.action_recommendation: Thoroughly review all RFQ requirements and ensure the quote is fully compliant before submission.

quotes.quote: Disqualify any Contractor whose Quote fails to conform to the requirements of the RFQ;

findings.title: Warranty Period Obligations
findings.fact: The document specifies warranty obligations, including replacement of inoperable units with new units and warranty coverage for docking stations and additional warranty years.
findings.business_implication: Warranty obligations are stringent, requiring new replacements and comprehensive coverage, which may increase costs but are essential for compliance.
findings.action_recommendation: Plan for warranty costs and ensure ability to provide new replacements and warranty SKUs for docking stations and additional years as required.

quotes.quote: If a unit becomes inoperable within the warranty window and cannot be repaired, a brand new unit shall be provided at no charge. Contractor shall not provide refurbished or remanufactured equipment as they are not allowed under this Aggregate Hardware Buy 23-01.
The Contractor is responsible for providing a warranty SKU(s) for docking stations listed as a Required Product or Additional Product on the price lists.
The Contractor is responsible for adding SKUs for additional warranty year options (e.g. 3 year, 4 year, 5 year) under Additional Products on Attachment A – Technical Response.

findings.title: OGS Not Liable for Bid Preparation Costs
findings.fact: OGS will not be held liable for any cost incurred by the Contractor for work performed in the preparation of a response to this RFQ.
findings.business_implication: The bidder bears all costs of preparing the response, with no reimbursement if not awarded.
findings.action_recommendation: Budget for bid preparation costs and ensure the investment is justified by the potential contract value.

quotes.quote: OGS will not be held liable for any cost incurred by the Contractor for work performed in the preparation of a response to this Request for Quote (RFQ).

findings.title: Contractor Assumes Risk for Timely Submission
findings.fact: Contractor assumes all risks for timely, properly submitted RFQ deliveries.
findings.business_implication: The bidder bears the risk of any delays or errors in submission, which could lead to rejection of the bid without recourse.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure a robust submission process with internal checks and early submission to mitigate the risk of late or improper delivery.

quotes.quote: Contractor assumes all risks for timely, properly submitted RFQ deliveries.

findings.title: No Guarantee of Volume or Dollar Value
findings.fact: There is no guarantee of volume or dollar value to be purchased under the resulting agreement.
findings.business_implication: The bidder cannot rely on estimated volumes or dollar values; actual purchases may be significantly lower, affecting revenue projections and resource allocation.
findings.action_recommendation: Price the proposal competitively while ensuring profitability even at lower volumes, and avoid over-committing resources based on estimates.

quotes.quote: There is no guarantee of volume to be purchased
There is no guarantee of dollar value to be purchased

findings.title: Contractor Must Furnish All Quantities Ordered
findings.fact: Contractor must furnish all quantities actually ordered by Authorized Users at or below the prices in the Agreement.
findings.business_implication: The bidder is obligated to supply any quantity ordered, even if demand exceeds expectations, which could strain supply chain and inventory.
findings.action_recommendation: Assess production capacity and supply chain robustness to ensure ability to meet potentially high demand, and include contingency plans for scaling up.

quotes.quote: Contractor must furnish all quantities actually ordered by Authorized Users at or below the prices in the Aggregate Hardware Buy 23-01 Agreement.

findings.title: Contractor Responsible for Replacement of Incompatible Components
findings.fact: Replacement components must be compatible with Agreement peripherals or the Contractor will be responsible for replacement of both the component and the peripheral.
findings.business_implication: If a replacement component is incompatible, the bidder incurs additional costs to replace both the component and the peripheral, increasing liability.
findings.action_recommendation: Thoroughly test replacement components for compatibility before offering them, and maintain a list of compatible peripherals to avoid such costs.

quotes.quote: Replacement components must be compatible with Agreement peripherals or the Contractor will be responsible for replacement of both the component and the peripheral.

findings.title: Contractor Responsible for Warranty SKUs for Docking Stations
findings.fact: The Contractor is responsible for providing a warranty SKU(s) for docking stations listed as a Required Product or Additional Product on the price lists. The warranty SKU(s) must fully cover hardware, software, and drivers.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must offer comprehensive warranty coverage for docking stations, which may increase costs and administrative burden.
findings.action_recommendation: Include warranty SKU costs in pricing and ensure that the warranty terms are clearly defined and manageable, possibly by partnering with manufacturers for support.

quotes.quote: The Contractor is responsible for providing a warranty SKU(s) for docking stations listed as a Required Product or Additional Product on the price lists. The warranty SKU(s) must fully cover hardware, software, and drivers.

findings.title: Termination for Repeated Failure to Comply
findings.fact: OGS may terminate an Agreement under this RFQ, in whole or in part, for Contractor's repeated failure to comply with any requirement under the Agreement.
findings.business_implication: This clause exposes the bidder to termination risk for any repeated non-compliance, even minor issues, which could lead to loss of the contract and revenue. It emphasizes the need for strict adherence to all contractual obligations.
findings.action_recommendation: Implement robust compliance monitoring and internal controls to ensure all requirements are consistently met. Designate a compliance officer to track obligations and address any issues promptly to avoid recurrence.

quotes.quote: Terminate an Agreement under this RFQ, in whole or in part, for Contractor’s repeated failure to comply with any requirement under the Agreement.
